candidates.text:
Standard: 1.P.EICC.2
Domain primary: Speaking & Listening
Domain secondary: Writing, Comprehension
Cognitive demand: DOK3_strategic_thinking
Competency: Engage in written or spoken conversations as both a speaker and listener for different tasks and purposes, making meaningful connections within and across texts and to real life.
Skills:
- Engage in spoken or written dialogue as an author and audience.
- Make intentional connections within texts.
- Make intentional connections between texts.
- Make intentional connections beyond texts to other knowledge or experiences.
Observable behaviors:
- Participate in dialogues by sharing ideas and responding to others.
- Make connections between different texts during discussions.
- Relate ideas from texts to personal experiences or other knowledge.
- Use spoken or written language intentionally to communicate for various purposes.
Pedagogy terms: dialogue, author and audience, text connections, purposeful communication
Required student actions:
- oral_production: Speak and respond in dialogues for different purposes.
- written_production: Write to communicate ideas and respond to texts.
- procedural_application: Use dialogue skills to connect ideas within and between texts.
- reasoning_explanation: Explain connections made between texts and ideas during dialogue.
- comprehension_response: Respond thoughtfully to texts and peers in spoken or written form.
Codes: 1.P.EICC.2
candidates.label: Engagement & Intention

candidates.text:
Standard: 1.P.AC.3.d
Domain primary: Speaking & Listening
Domain secondary: Writing, Comprehension
Cognitive demand: DOK3_strategic_thinking
Competency: Use and understand multimodal texts that combine different genres, text features, and craft techniques to influence audiences and achieve specific purposes.
Skills:
- Consume multimodal texts that integrate various genres, text features, and craft techniques.
- Produce multimodal texts that combine genres, text features, and craft techniques to influence target audiences and achieve specific purposes.
Observable behaviors:
- Identify different genres within multimodal texts.
- Recognize and describe various text features in multimodal texts.
- Explain how craft techniques affect the audience and purpose of a text.
- Create multimodal texts that combine genres, text features, and craft techniques to influence a target audience.
- Use multimodal elements to achieve a specific purpose in communication.
Pedagogy terms: multimodal texts, genres, text features, craft techniques, audience, purpose
Required student actions:
- recognition_identification: Identify genres, text features, and craft techniques in multimodal texts.
- written_production: Produce multimodal texts that integrate genres, text features, and craft techniques to influence audiences and purposes.
- procedural_application: Use knowledge of text design to create multimodal texts for specific audiences and purposes.
- reasoning_explanation: Explain how different genres, text features, and craft techniques influence the audience and purpose of multimodal texts.
- comprehension_response: Respond to multimodal texts by discussing how their design affects audience and purpose.
Codes: 1.P.AC.3.d

Standard: 1.P.EICC.1.e
Domain primary: Speaking & Listening
Domain secondary: Writing, Comprehension
Cognitive demand: DOK2_skills_concepts
Competency: Participate actively in a community of readers and writers by following group norms, discussing texts, sharing writing, listening to others, and giving and receiving feedback.
Skills:
- Develop group norms for participation in a community of readers and writers
- Discuss texts with others in the group
- Share individual writing with the group
- Listen to others as they share their writing
- Offer feedback on peers' writing
- Respond to feedback received on own writing
Observable behaviors:
- Follow agreed-upon group norms during reading and writing activities
- Discuss texts with peers by sharing ideas and listening to others
- Share individual writing pieces with the group
- Listen attentively as others share their writing
- Offer constructive feedback on peers' writing
- Respond appropriately to feedback received on own writing
Pedagogy terms: community of readers and writers, group norms, discussion, sharing writing, listening, feedback
Required student actions:
- oral_production: Discuss texts with peers and share writing aloud
- procedural_application: Follow group norms during reading and writing activities
- reasoning_explanation: Offer and respond to feedback on writing
- comprehension_response: Listen attentively to others' writing and participate in text discussions
Codes: 1.P.EICC.1.e

Standard: 1.P.CP.1.d
Domain primary: Speaking & Listening
Domain secondary: Comprehension, Writing
Cognitive demand: DOK3_strategic_thinking
Competency: Work together with others to talk about topics, ask and investigate questions, solve problems, and explore and create texts.
Skills:
- Work with others to discuss topics.
- Work with others to investigate questions.
- Work with others to solve problems.
- Work with others to explore and create texts.
Observable behaviors:
- Participate in group discussions about various topics.
- Ask and investigate questions collaboratively.
- Work with peers to solve problems.
- Explore and create texts together with others.
Pedagogy terms: collaboration, discussion, problem solving, text exploration, text creation
Required student actions:
- oral_production: Contribute ideas and questions during group discussions.
- procedural_application: Work cooperatively with others to discuss topics, investigate questions, solve problems, and create texts.
- investigation_handson: Engage in collaborative inquiry and problem solving with peers.
- reasoning_explanation: Explain ideas and reasoning during group work.
- comprehension_response: Respond to and build on others' ideas in discussions.
Codes: 1.P.CP.1.d

Standard: 1.T.C.1
Domain primary: Comprehension
Domain secondary: Writing, Speaking & Listening
Cognitive demand: DOK2_skills_concepts
Competency: Explain how authors use language to achieve a specific purpose and address a target audience, and create texts in various modes.
Skills:
- Identify the general purpose of a variety of texts.
- Identify the target audience of a variety of texts.
- Identify different modes of communication: print, digital, auditory, and visual.
- Create texts in teacher-selected modes such as print, digital, auditory, and/or visual.
Observable behaviors:
- Identify the general purpose of a text, such as telling stories, providing information, sharing opinions, or explaining ideas.
- Recognize the target audience for different texts.
- Identify different modes of communication including print, digital, auditory, and visual.
- Create texts using teacher-selected modes such as print, digital, auditory, or visual formats.
Pedagogy terms: purpose, audience, modes of communication, text creation
Required student actions:
- recognition_identification: Identify the general purpose and target audience in various texts and recognize different modes of communication.
- written_production: Create texts in teacher-selected modes such as print or digital.
- representation_modeling: Create texts in teacher-selected modes including auditory and visual formats.
- reasoning_explanation: Explain how authors use language for a specific purpose and target audience.
Codes: 1.T.C.1
candidates.label: Purpose & Audience

candidates.text:
Standard: 1.P.EICC.2.d
Domain primary: Comprehension
Domain secondary: Writing, Speaking & Listening
Cognitive demand: DOK3_strategic_thinking
Competency: Interpret and create texts to help analyze and evaluate texts and ideas.
Skills:
- Interpret texts to analyze ideas.
- Construct texts to evaluate ideas.
Observable behaviors:
- Explain the meaning of texts in their own words.
- Create texts that express their understanding of ideas.
- Use texts to compare and think critically about ideas.
Pedagogy terms: interpretation, text construction, analysis, evaluation, ideas, author and audience
Required student actions:
- recognition_identification: Identify ideas and information in texts to support analysis and evaluation.
- oral_production: Explain interpretations and evaluations of texts orally.
- written_production: Create written texts that express analysis and evaluation of ideas.
- procedural_application: Use texts intentionally to analyze and evaluate ideas.
- representation_modeling: Construct texts that represent understanding of ideas.
- reasoning_explanation: Explain reasoning behind interpretations and evaluations of texts.
- comprehension_response: Respond to texts by interpreting and evaluating ideas.
Codes: 1.P.EICC.2.d

Standard: 1.P.EICC.4.c
Domain primary: Writing
Domain secondary: Speaking & Listening, Comprehension
Cognitive demand: DOK2_skills_concepts
Competency: Generate ideas for writing by using what they already know, gathering information from texts, and talking with others.
Skills:
- Generate ideas for writing by assessing prior knowledge.
- Generate ideas for writing by gathering information from texts.
- Generate ideas for writing by engaging in discussions with others.
Observable behaviors:
- Recall and use prior knowledge to think of writing topics.
- Find information in texts to help develop writing ideas.
- Participate in discussions to share and develop ideas for writing.
Pedagogy terms: generate ideas, prior knowledge, gather information, discussions, writing process
Required student actions:
- recognition_identification: Identify prior knowledge relevant to a writing topic.
- oral_production: Participate in discussions to share ideas for writing.
- procedural_application: Use prior knowledge and information from texts to generate ideas for writing.
- reasoning_explanation: Explain how prior knowledge, information from texts, and discussions help generate writing ideas.
- comprehension_response: Gather information from texts to support writing ideas.
Codes: 1.P.EICC.4.c

Standard: 1.L.V.1
Domain primary: Vocabulary
Domain secondary: Speaking & Listening, Writing
Cognitive demand: DOK2_skills_concepts
Competency: Students acquire and use general, academic, and specialized vocabulary words and phrases in different settings.
Skills:
- Acquire general, academic, and specialized vocabulary words and phrases through grade-level texts and content.
- Use grade-level general, academic, and specialized vocabulary words and phrases to communicate in a variety of settings.
Observable behaviors:
- Identify and learn new vocabulary words from grade-level texts and content.
- Use vocabulary words appropriately when speaking and writing in various contexts.
Pedagogy terms: vocabulary acquisition, academic vocabulary, specialized vocabulary, word usage, communication
Required student actions:
- recognition_identification: Recognize and identify general, academic, and specialized vocabulary words in grade-level texts and content.
- oral_production: Use general, academic, and specialized vocabulary words correctly when speaking in different settings.
- written_production: Use general, academic, and specialized vocabulary words correctly when writing in different settings.
- procedural_application: Apply vocabulary knowledge to understand and communicate ideas in various contexts.
Codes: 1.L.V.1

Standard: 1.P.EICC.1
Domain primary: Comprehension
Domain secondary: Writing, Speaking & Listening
Cognitive demand: DOK3_strategic_thinking
Competency: Build a personal identity as a reader and writer by developing and using a variety of skills, strategies, and tools to actively engage with and create texts.
Skills:
- Generate, understand, monitor, and revise personal and academic reading and writing goals.
- Discuss or write about personal and academic reading and writing preferences with reference to specific techniques, topics, modes, and genres.
- Select, read, and write texts of personal interest and academic relevance.
- Build and draw from a repertoire of comprehension and composition skills, strategies, and techniques to interpret and construct texts.
- Participate in a community of readers and writers by developing group norms, discussing texts, sharing writing, listening to others, and offering and responding to feedback.
- Develop independence and autonomy as a reader and writer.
Observable behaviors:
- Set and revise personal and academic reading and writing goals.
- Discuss or write about reading and writing preferences with examples of techniques, topics, modes, and genres.
- Choose and engage with texts that interest them and relate to academic topics.
- Use a range of comprehension and composition strategies to understand and create texts.
- Participate in group discussions about texts and writing, share their own writing, listen to others, and give and receive feedback.
- Demonstrate growing independence in reading and writing tasks.
Pedagogy terms: reading goals, writing goals, reading preferences, writing preferences, text selection, comprehension strategies, composition strategies, collaborative discussion, feedback, reader identity, writer identity, independence
Required student actions:
- oral_production: Discuss reading and writing preferences and participate in group discussions about texts and writing.
- written_production: Write about personal and academic reading and writing preferences and share individual writing.
- procedural_application: Set, monitor, and revise personal and academic reading and writing goals; select and use comprehension and composition strategies as needed.
- reasoning_explanation: Explain personal and academic reading and writing preferences referring to specific techniques, topics, modes, and genres.
- comprehension_response: Respond to texts by participating in discussions, sharing writing, and offering and responding to feedback.
Codes: 1.P.EICC.1
candidates.label: Reader & Writer Identity

candidates.text:
Standard: 1.P.EICC.2.a
Domain primary: Writing
Domain secondary: Speaking & Listening
Cognitive demand: DOK2_skills_concepts
Competency: Tell or share real or imagined experiences by creating or interpreting stories in spoken or written form.
Skills:
- Share real experiences by telling or writing stories.
- Share imagined experiences by telling or writing stories.
- Interpret stories that tell or include real or imagined experiences.
Observable behaviors:
- Tell a story about something that really happened or something made up.
- Create a story by drawing or writing.
- Listen to or read a story and explain what happened.
- Share stories with others through speaking or writing.
Pedagogy terms: storytelling, narrative, experience sharing, interpretation, composition
Required student actions:
- oral_production: Tell or share stories about real or imagined experiences orally.
- written_production: Write or draw stories that tell about real or imagined experiences.
- comprehension_response: Interpret stories to understand real or imagined experiences.
Codes: 1.P.EICC.2.a
